clue.text: Extraordinary glories around a part of palace

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go on both sides of the single letter a
extraordinary describes something out of the usual order, so the letters of glories are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admires the remarkable splendours surrounding one wing of a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' turns GLORIES into SERGLIO, and 'around' puts that either side of A: SER-A-GLIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of an Ottoman palace, the harem, so it is one section of such a building.

clue.text: Relative dismay when date is off

indicators.note: is off means has gone away, so the letter for date is removed from the longer word

parts.note: to dismay someone is to daunt them, discouraging them

explanation.surface: A family member is upset when a planned appointment gets cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is off' takes D out of DAUNT, leaving the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family member.

clue.text: Sweet drama, upper-class piece

parts.note: No (also Noh) is classical Japanese drama
U is the old label for upper-class usage
piece is slang for a gun, as is gat

explanation.surface: A theatre production with a posh scene in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' is gangster slang for a handgun, and so is GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts, a kind of candy.

clue.text: Commotion rising round

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Commotion rising round (8)' looks cut short: STIR reversed gives RITS, and nothing in the remaining words supplies the DENT or a definition for TRIDENTS

clue.text: Ace and King held by cheat? That's striking

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: held by means the king's name sits inside the word for a cheat

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick, a swindle
Saul was the first king of Israel

explanation.surface: In a card game, holding the top cards lets a swindler win big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' is not K here but SAUL, the Old Testament king; 'held by' puts him inside STING after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaulting someone is hitting or attacking them, so it means striking.

clue.text: Mind occupied by mass on large mountain

indicators.note: occupied by says the word for mass moves into the word for mind

parts.note: to mind is to care, as in 'I don't mind'
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone's thoughts are filled with a church service held on a big peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupied by' puts M inside CARE, giving CAME, and L for large follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Carmel is a coastal ridge in northern Israel, famous from the story of Elijah.

clue.text: Shapeless English volume with ending lacking in sense

indicators.note: in says these letters sit inside the word for sense

parts.note: nous is common sense, gumption

indicators.note: with ending lacking says the final letter of the word for volume is dropped

parts.note: volume as amount is bulk

explanation.surface: A thick English book seems to have no proper conclusion and makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a book, but it means BULK; 'with ending lacking' trims it to BUL, and E plus BUL go 'in' NOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulous means hazy and vague, without a clear form, like a cloud.

clue.text: Hit, man gets bandage

parts.note: to swat is to hit, as with a fly
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone is struck, and the man is given a dressing for the wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap something up in cloth, just as a bandage binds a wound.

clue.text: Rogue with nasty scar going by name of Capone

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of scar are messed up into a new order

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster, so his first name gives Al

explanation.surface: A gangster with an ugly mark on his face goes by the name Capone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges SCAR to RASC, and Al Capone's first name follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a scoundrel, a dishonest or mischievous person.

clue.text: Desire unrestrained? Not on

indicators.note: Not tells us to leave out the word on from the longer word

parts.note: wanton behaviour is unrestrained, unruly

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a longing is wild, and is told it is not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' removes ON from WANTON.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to wish or long for it.

clue.text: Member of family in third grade seizing chance, missing nothing

indicators.note: seizing says the grade grabs the other letters and holds them inside

parts.note: gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet, used as a third-class grade

indicators.note: missing tells us the letter for nothing is dropped from the word for chance

parts.note: random means by chance, haphazard
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A relative in the third year of school grabs an opportunity but ends up with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A gamma is a third-class mark (after alpha and beta); 'missing' drops O from RANDOM, and 'seizing' puts RANDM inside GAMMA after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmamma is a grandmother, a parent's mother, which makes her a relative.

clue.text: Unfashionable lot had to be given makeover

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, so the letters of lot had are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dowdy collection of possessions needs a new look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be given makeover' rearranges LOT HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is out of date and tired, no longer in style.

clue.text: Servant, one in demand, working after hours

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the abbreviation for hours

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: working means being worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A domestic who is much sought after keeps busy late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges A, IN and DEMAND into ANDMAIDEN, which comes 'after' H.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaiden is a female attendant, a maid serving a mistress.

clue.text: House, one that's far from outstanding, in state capital

parts.note: a lulu is an outstanding example of something, so something ordinary is no lulu

explanation.surface: A home, nothing special, in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lulu' is a remarkable or outstanding thing, so an unremarkable one is 'no lulu'.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu, on Oahu, is the capital of Hawaii, a US state.

clue.text: What's revolutionary in design, in wood, is having…

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the run is read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the run of words design, in wood

explanation.surface: A radical approach to carving wood is the property of someone; the clue runs on into the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 17 Across. 'in' points to letters within DESIGN, IN WOOD, and 'revolutionary' reads GNINWO backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning something means possessing it, which is the same as having it.

clue.text: Edges of numerous answers, reading clockwise, impart suggestion song implausibly plants

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Edges of numerous answers, reading clockwise, impart suggestion song implausibly plants (8)' is garbled OCR mixing what seems to be a puzzle note with the clue; no parse gives NARCISSI from it
annotationWithheld.clue: Edges of numerous answers, reading clockwise, impart suggestion song implausibly plants

clue.text: … appealing surface covered with silver

indicators.note: covered with says the word for silver goes round the word for surface

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
skin is an outer surface, as on fruit

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone admires an attractive coating plated with silver.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 15 Across. 'covered with' wraps AG round SKIN: A-SKIN-G.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking means requesting or pleading, the begging sense of appealing.

clue.text: Good, experienced director is about to get sales-related award

parts.note: old means seasoned, experienced
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A veteran film-maker of quality is set to receive a prize for box-office success.
explanation.walkthrough: C is circa, about, used before dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold disc is presented to a recording artist when a record reaches a set sales figure.

clue.text: End with spirit

definitions.meaning: to end something abruptly, as in stopping a rumour
a distilled alcoholic drink such as whisky

explanation.surface: Someone finishes off a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan or rumour is to stop it dead; Scotch is also the whisky made in Scotland, a distilled drink.

clue.text: Rotten cruet found to contain little room for condiment

indicators.note: to contain says the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation for room inside them
rotten suggests something decayed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the printed fodder cruet is taken with the I the setter left out, since the answer needs six letters around the room abbreviation
RM is the short form of room

explanation.surface: A spoiled container for oil and vinegar turns out to have a bit of space for a spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' rearranges the fodder into TUERIC and 'to contain' puts RM inside: TU-RM-ERIC. As printed CRUET lacks the I the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is a yellow spice ground from a root, used to flavour and colour food.

clue.text: Remove blockage from end of drain, breaking up projecting part

indicators.note: breaking means cutting into, so that letter splits the word up
end of picks out the final letter of the word drain

parts.note: a lug is a projecting part such as an ear or handle

explanation.surface: A plumber clears a pipe by working at the end of the drain and pulling out a sticking-out bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' picks N from DRAIN, which goes 'breaking' UP to make UNP; LUG follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplug is to take out a stopper or clear an obstruction.

clue.text: Obtain a lot of extra rolls

parts.note: to bag something is to get hold of it

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter of the word for extra goes

parts.note: else means other, additional, as in 'anything else'

explanation.surface: Someone gets a large number of spare bread buns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes most of ELSE, dropping its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagels are ring-shaped bread rolls, boiled then baked.

clue.text: Got endlessly interrupted by learner, put into inert condition

indicators.note: interrupted by means the learner letter breaks into the shortened word
endlessly says the word for got loses its last letter

parts.note: got as in 'got angry' means became
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A trainee keeps cutting in until the speaker becomes sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BECAME to BECAM, and 'interrupted by' puts L in before the final M.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm is to leave a ship motionless for lack of wind, and so to make still.

clue.text: Positive mass of droplets I observed in device for measuring liquid

indicators.note: in says the letters go inside the word for the measuring device

parts.note: an optic is the measure fixed to an upturned spirit bottle in a bar
mist is a cloud of tiny water droplets

explanation.surface: Someone looking at fog through a scientific gauge is hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: In British bars an OPTIC is the dispenser that measures a single shot of spirits; I and MIST go 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being optimistic is being hopeful, confident about the future.

clue.text: Dress made by one in 1501

indicators.note: in says the numeral for one sits inside the numerals for the year

parts.note: in Roman numerals 1501 is MDI
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gown dating from the sixteenth century.
explanation.walkthrough: MDI is 1000 + 500 + 1; 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A midi is a dress or skirt reaching to mid-calf.

clue.text: Reproduction instant? Certainly not

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
no is a flat refusal

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a copy can be made right away and is refused.
explanation.definitionFit: Mono is single-channel sound reproduction, as opposed to stereo.

clue.text: Containers loaded with King Edward potatoes?

indicators.note: loaded with says the containers have the royal letters put inside them

parts.note: tubs are containers
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: Bins are filled with King Edwards, a well-known British potato variety.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato, but here it is ER, Edward the King.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes are swollen underground stems, examples of plant storage organs; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Rows among crowd with no time for piety

indicators.note: among says the rows go in between the letters of the shortened crowd
with no says the letter for time is dropped from the word for crowd

parts.note: a host is a great crowd, a multitude
lines are rows

explanation.surface: Lines of worshippers in a congregation with no time to spare for devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops T from HOST to give HOS; 'among' puts LINES inside: HO-LINES-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiness is saintliness, the quality of being devout and sacred.
